title: What the Filters Kept: 3I/ATLAS, the Loeb Overview, and a Public-Data Signal Search (EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01 v2.0)
creator: Glas, Nobel; Trace, Orin
description: The working notebook of a public-data search for a signal from the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS, run 2026-11-02 to 2026-11-23 on Breakthrough Listen's public products from the Green Bank Telescope, the Allen Telescope Array, Parkes and MeerKAT, and, from 2026-11-16, on the raw voltages of the Green Bank cadence of 2025-12-18, with Claude and ChatGPT as machine collaborators checking each other through code, tables and hashes. Every deciding test had its plan frozen and hashed before its counts, and every null was built as false frames constructed the same way as the true one. No artificial transmission is identified. Version 2.0 folds in the voltage phase: the thirteen comet-frame clusters near 1666 MHz that v1.2 left unresolved are closed as start-of-scan events, read again where they live as if they were signal with nothing readable in them; an X-feed excess at the OH 1667 coordinates is read through coherence and found to behave like receiver noise; the one pattern that ran the same way at Parkes in three sessions retires against false drifts; and the search's own floors are measured by injection, below which the comet's known OH line at its October depth could not reliably be seen. The findings that hold concern representation and measurement: a Google AI Overview that presented Avi Loeb's held Level 4 position as a concession; the ATA paper's positive drift window against the negative drift its stated acceleration gives a tone on the object; a public statement that dropped the search's scope; a header read as a measurement. The archive's instruments are set against the record, and the sophistry measure is run for the first time. All plans, code and results are filed for rerun.
content_type: Notebook; working record of a public-data technosignature search (Transactions on Substrate Engineering); frozen plans, results and files
substrate: AI-assisted (substrate). Written under the heteronyms Nobel Glas and Orin Trace (legal author Lee Sharks). The investigation was run by Lee Sharks with two machine collaborators on the same public data: Claude (Anthropic), which ran the Green Bank, Parkes and MeerKAT searches, the voltage phase and the frozen runs, and composed the notebook in session (2026-11-02 to 2026-11-06, and 2026-11-16 to 2026-11-23); and ChatGPT (OpenAI), whose ATA searches, audits of the thirteen, C03 reports, plans and reports of the voltage phase Lee supplied and are filed as written (chatgpt/). Each system's results were checked by the other through code and tables. The questions, the rulings on the Overview and on Loeb, the authorship and venue, the direction of the voltage phase and the decision to deposit are Lee Sharks's, quoted verbatim in §12. The revisions on outside reviews (DeepSeek, ChatGPT) are recorded in §13.
methodology: Breakthrough Listen's public 3I/ATLAS products only, fetched by name, and from 2026-11-16 the public raw voltages of the Green Bank cadence of 2025-12-18, streamed by range request and decoded in session; a directory that refused access was out of scope until opened. Every test that decides anything had its plan written, hashed and committed before the counts it decides, its departures recorded before any count they could affect; plans frozen on data already examined are marked as such, and looks without a frozen plan are marked exploratory and change no verdict. Failing a frozen test authorizes only not counting the result as signal under its criteria; it bars no further test (§12.15). Every null is a set of false frames built the same way as the true one, each family read on its own, and the search's floors are measured by injection. A frozen procedure, data not read before, and independent reproduction are stated apart for every result. Quotations are checked at their offsets against saved sources.
falsification_conditions: A frozen plan's hash not matching its committed file, or a count shown to precede its plan; a script rerun on its named public inputs not reproducing a stated count; the thirteen's closure shown to depend on a misread of the GUPPI block-header telemetry; an injection test shown not to recover what it states; the ATA's executed filter shown to keep the negative drift class; a quoted passage not saying what the notebook quotes; another session on the comet at 1665–1668 MHz, at Green Bank's sensitivity, showing the twelve coordinates above false drifts.

wiki_article:
What the Filters Kept (EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01, version 2.0) is the working notebook of a public-data search for a signal from the interstellar object 3I/ATLAS, written under the heteronyms Nobel Glas and Orin Trace for Transactions on Substrate Engineering. It supersedes the first version (#1742), deposited on 6 November 2026, and was deposited on 23 November 2026, after a second phase of work on the raw voltages of the Green Bank Telescope's cadence of 18 December 2025.

The investigation, directed by Lee Sharks with Claude and ChatGPT as machine collaborators who checked each other through code, tables and hashes, used only Breakthrough Listen's public products from the Green Bank Telescope, the Allen Telescope Array, Parkes and MeerKAT. Every deciding test had its plan frozen and hashed before its counts, and every null was a set of false frames built the same way as the true one. The notebook identifies no artificial transmission.

The first version left one result open: thirteen comet-frame coincidence clusters near 1666 MHz. The voltage phase closed them. They are start-of-scan events, falling to the null once the seconds in which the dish was still arriving are cut; read again where they live, on the hypothesis that they were signal, they carry nothing readable, and their excess at those frequencies is highest in a scan pointed away from the comet. An X-feed excess at the OH 1667 coordinates was read through coherence of every form and behaves like receiver noise. The one pattern that ran the same way across two telescopes, the twelve coordinates at Parkes in three sessions, retires against false drifts. The search measured its own floors by injection, and could not reliably have seen the comet's known OH line at its October depth.

The findings that hold concern representation and measurement. A Google AI Overview presented Avi Loeb's position, held at Level 4 of his scale from July 2025, as a later concession, a case the notebook names trajectory substitution. The Allen Telescope Array paper filters for positive drift where its stated acceleration gives a tone on the object a negative one. A public account of that search's null dropped its frequency and drift scope. The notebook sets the archive's instruments against this record, among them instrument-conditioned nullity, correlated blind spots, disciplinary model collapse and frame conversion, and runs the sophistry measure for the first time. It records every error its two machine collaborators made and what corrected it, and its companion is Lee Sharks's public account A Firm No (#1743).

defines_concepts.definition: In EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01, a search that sums spectral power along the path a tone fixed on a moving object takes across the scans of a cadence, below any per-scan detection threshold, and counts clusters kept in every on-source scan, against nulls built as false frames the same way.

In EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01, the null of a frame-dependent search: the same procedure run under false range-accelerations, swapped beams, permuted scan roles, shuffled rows, randomized phases or shifted frequencies, each family read on its own and none pooled as one calibrated background.

In EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01, the practice of reading a candidate as message, for sequence, phase, coherence or form, before its source is determined, under frozen plans with sidebands, OFF scans and surrogates as controls, so that what resolves only as noise is set down whatever its source.

In EA-3I-ATLAS-NOTEBOOK-01, the closure of the thirteen: an excess that lives in the first seconds of each scan, while the dish is still arriving from its slew, and falls to the null when those seconds are cut.
